# Buffered fixed-face contact minima and affine-invariant continuation

This is a finite, actual-body continuation theorem. It upgrades the
fixed-face cover in
`candidate 86dd5366456916a8`
and the inward continuation audited in
`unshared historical review/context (not an accepted premise)`.
It does not prove a signed payment inequality or an outer minimizing
body theorem.

The first part needs only compatible fixed-base Hausdorff-continuous
body paths. The derivative part requires a stated bounded radial first
variation and regular selected cap traces. Neither nesting nor a
continued path of deepest points is assumed.

## 1. Fixed original family and its invariant buffered groups

Let d>=1, N=d+1, and let P be a finite lattice-complete set with positive
compatible convex fibers K_z. Work on its canonical hull. Put

    M=sum_z |K_z|,
    Sigma=(1/M)sum_z integral_(K_z)(X-g_z)(X-g_z)^T dX,
    Gamma(u)=sqrt(u^T Sigma u),
    f(z,x)=(E_(K_z)(x)/M)^(1/N)

at integer bases, with the same canonical-fiber definition at real
bases. The covariance is WITHIN each fiber. Sigma is positive definite.
The buffer uses the homogeneous threshold

    a.(Z-z)+u.(X-x) >= -epsilon f(z,x) Gamma(u),

along with unchanged closed pure-base caps. Fix epsilon>0 sufficiently
small that every actual buffered maximizer has a proper shifted own
section. Let Q be the maximal raw buffered depth, beta=Q/M, and let I
be its maximizing integer bases.

The audited buffered theorem supplies at most k(I)<=k(P) fixed witness
groups. For group i choose one old maximizing source (p_i,y_i), its
minimal deepest-base face F_i, and at most d+1 caps with fixed normals

    N_ij=(a_ij,u_ij),  Gamma(u_ij)=1,
    H_ij={N_ij.(Z,X)>=c_ij},  mu(H_ij)=Q,
    rho_ij>0,  sum_j rho_ij=1.

Write

    h_i=sum_j rho_ij c_ij,
    J_i=I intersect F_i,
    P_i(z,x)=sum_j rho_ij N_ij.(z,x).

The sets J_i cover I; they may overlap. Lattice completeness implies
that J_i is all integer bases on F_i. The full-supergradient argument
gives the exact inequality

    psi_i0(z,x):=P_i(z,x)-h_i-epsilon f(z,x) >=0
                  for z in F_i, x in K_z.                         (1)

For f=E^(1/N), the equality theorem gives more. Every z in J_i has a
UNIQUE zero y_z of psi_i0(z,.) on K_z. It is interior. All marked
fibers K_z-y_z, z in J_i, are identical; in particular their energies

    E_z(y_z)=E_i>0,     f(z,y_z)=f_i=(E_i/M)^(1/N)                  (2)

are equal. The marks form the restriction of an affine graph on F_i.
The uniqueness includes boundary points: a second tangent contact
would force affinity along an interior segment, contrary to strict
fixed-body concavity of E^(1/N). These facts do not assert equality
between different groups.

## 2. An exact contact minimum for arbitrary nearby compatible paths

Let K_z(t) be positive compatible convex bodies on the SAME bases P,
with K_z(t)->K_z in Hausdorff distance as t decreases to zero. No nesting
is assumed. Let mu_t,M_t,Sigma_t,Gamma_t,f_t be the actual updated
quantities, with

    f_t(z,x)=(E_(K_z(t))(x)/M_t)^(1/N).

Keep all old normals and weights fixed, and define

    A_i(t)=sum_j rho_ij Gamma_t(u_ij),
    alpha_i(t)=min_(z in J_i, x in K_z(t))
        [P_i(z,x)-h_i-epsilon A_i(t) f_t(z,x)].                    (3)

This is a minimum over a FINITE collection of compact actual fibers.
It uses the updated continuous-normal norm, so A_i(0)=1. The value
alpha_i(t) may be positive or negative.

Continuity of fiber volume, first and second moments, and marked
energy implies

    A_i(t)->1,       alpha_i(t)->0.                               (4)

For clarity, the minimizing points converge to the finite old contact
set {(z,y_z):z in J_i}. A minimizing sequence has a subsequence with
fixed base and convergent continuous point. Hausdorff convergence puts
its limit in the old fiber; marked energy continuity and (1) make its
limiting value nonnegative. Testing the old interior marks, which
remain in the new fibers for small t, makes the limit at most zero.
Uniqueness in (1) identifies the limiting point as y_z. This argument
does not presume a first-order rate for the minimizing points.

Let c_ij(t,q) be the RIGHT upper q-quantile of the actual new measure
in the fixed normal N_ij. The old own trace is proper. In a neighborhood
of (t,q)=(0,Q), cap-volume convergence and that own trace give continuous
quantiles, strictly decreasing in q. Thus the scalar equation

    sum_j rho_ij c_ij(t,q_i(t)) = h_i+alpha_i(t)                   (5)

has a unique nearby solution, and q_i(t)->Q. It is enough to bracket
Q by two fixed nearby masses and use the intermediate value theorem;
no smooth quantile inverse is needed for this exact statement.

For every z in J_i and x in K_z(t), equations (3) and (5) give

    sum_j rho_ij [N_ij.(z,x)-c_ij(t,q_i(t))
                         -epsilon f_t(z,x) Gamma_t(u_ij)] >=0.   (6)

At least one term is nonnegative. The actual buffered cap at (z,x)
in that normal therefore lies INSIDE the corresponding fixed-normal
cap of mass q_i(t). Consequently

    b_(epsilon,t)(z,x) <= q_i(t),     z in J_i.                    (7)

This includes all new source choices in these fibers, not only the
old marks or a presumed differentiable maximizing-source path.

The remaining sampled bases have a strict old gap below Q. That gap
persists by joint upper semicontinuity. Indeed for a convergent actual
source sequence, every fixed nonvertical buffered cap has convergent
mass: fiber indicator functions converge in volume, energy is continuous
at the marked limit including its zero boundary value, and covariance
and M are continuous. Every fixed pure-base CLOSED cap is upper
semicontinuous. Taking their infimum proves the asserted joint upper
semicontinuity. Compactness in each of finitely many nondeepest fibers
then preserves a common strict gap. Since q_i(t)->Q, for small t

    max_(w in S_t) b_(epsilon,t)(w) <= max_i q_i(t).               (8)

Thus (3)--(8) are an exact fixed-parity witness cover for ANY compatible
fixed-base Hausdorff-continuous path. They do not use f_t<=f_0 or
Sigma_t<=Sigma_0.

## 3. Sufficient physical first-variation hypotheses

Here is a concrete sufficient class for the derivative statements.
In each fiber choose an old interior radial origin o_z. Write its old
and new radial functions on the unit sphere as R_z and R_z,t. Suppose
the bodies remain convex and, for some uniform constant C,

    |R_z,t(omega)-R_z(omega)| <= C t,
    [R_z,t(omega)-R_z(omega)]/t -> r_z(omega)
                                      for sphere-almost every omega. (9)

The limit r_z is bounded and may have either sign. In d=1 the sphere
has its two counting-measure points. At a regular boundary point
X=o_z+R_z(omega)omega define its signed INWARD normal speed by

    v_z(X)=-r_z(omega) n_z(X).omega.

An old inner ball gives n_z.omega bounded away from zero almost
everywhere. The radial surface formula yields, for continuous h,

    d/dt|_0 integral_(K_z(t)) h
           =-integral_(boundary K_z) h(X)v_z(X)dS.                (10)

The convergence in (10) is uniform for a uniformly bounded, uniformly
Lipschitz family of integrands on a common compact neighborhood.
To verify this, use signed oriented radial shell integrals. Replacing
their integrand by its old endpoint value has error O(t^2) uniformly;
the remaining error is bounded by a constant times
integral|[R_z,t-R_z]/t-r_z|, which tends to zero by bounded dominated
convergence. Thus no C2 body boundary is required.

Assume additionally that every selected old cap admits the regular
joint threshold/shape expansion

    mu_t{N_ij.W>=c_ij+t s}
       =Q-t[L_ij+S_ij s]+o(t),                                  (11)

uniformly for bounded s, with S_ij>0. Here L_ij is its ACTUAL fixed
closed-cap first loss and S_ij the mixed coarea, including the divisor
||u_ij||. A sufficient status condition is that every fiber cut be
proper, strict full, or strict empty. Supporting traces of zero surface
measure are also harmless under the usual coarea limits. Positive-area
supporting facets require their coupled inside/outside selectors;
equation (11) is not asserted for them without that extra analysis.

The hypotheses (9) and (11) are additional to Hausdorff continuity.
They hold for the bounded radial action classes already proved in the
global-cut construction, when its selected cap traces are regular.

## 4. Uniform energy envelopes near the finite contact marks

The signed uniform envelope and finite-contact argument were also
proved independently in Sections 1--4 of
`candidate d750a370b2e831ee`;
the independent audit is
`unshared historical review/context (not an accepted premise)`.
The proof below spells out the hypotheses needed in this application.

Let U be a compact neighborhood of an old interior mark, contained in
the interior of its fiber. For y in U let a_y be the unique old energy
minimizer and put L_y(X)=1+a_y.(X-y). Under (9), uniformly for y in U,

    E_(K_z(t))(y)=E_(K_z)(y)-t C_z(y)+o(t),
    C_z(y)=integral_(boundary K_z) L_y(X)^(-N)v_z(X)dS.            (12)

Here are the parameter-uniformity details. Common inner balls for all
marks in U and the optimal denominator floor 1/N bound all old and new
optimizers a_t(y). Their denominators on the OLD body are at least
1/N-O(t), hence at least 1/(2N) for small t. The corresponding objective
kernels form a uniformly bounded Lipschitz family on a common compact
neighborhood. Formula (10) therefore gives their uniform objective
expansion. Uniform convergence of a_t(y) to a_y follows by compactness
and uniqueness: any contrary sequence has a convergent mark and
optimizer subsequence, whose limit minimizes the old objective at that
mark. Continuity of the old unique minimizer gives a contradiction.
Evaluating the new objective at the old optimizer, and the old
objective at the new optimizer, then sandwiches the difference by
(12). The kernel loss is continuous in (a,y), so replacing a_t(y) by
a_y in that loss is uniform. This proves (12) without interchanging an
uncontrolled infimum and a derivative.

Set

    D=sum_z integral_(boundary K_z) v_z dS,       dot M=-D.

Taking the smooth positive power and dividing by M_t gives uniformly
near these marks

    f_t(z,y)=f(z,y)+t dot f_body(z,y)+o(t),
    dot f_body(z,y)=f(z,y)/N [-C_z(y)/E_z(y)+D/M].                 (13)

The normalization term D/M is essential and can have either sign in
a signed path.

## 5. The finite-contact derivative, including covariance

The updated within-fiber covariance has the exact derivative

    dot Sigma=(D Sigma-J)/M,
    J=sum_z integral_(boundary K_z)
                       (X-g_z)(X-g_z)^T v_z(X)dS.                (14)

Terms from differentiating g_z vanish because the old first centered
moment is zero. Since Gamma(u_ij)=1,

    dot A_i=(1/2)sum_j rho_ij u_ij^T dot Sigma u_ij.               (15)

Use (12)--(13) and (15) in the objective defining alpha_i. They give a
uniform first-order expansion near every old contact mark. The finite
minimum envelope now gives

    dot alpha_i
       =min_(z in J_i) {-epsilon [dot A_i f_i
                                      +dot f_body(z,y_z)]}
       =epsilon f_i [ min_(z in J_i) C_z(y_z)/(N E_i)
                                      -D/(N M)-dot A_i].         (16)

There is no hidden differentiability assumption on the new minimizing
mark. For the upper bound test each fixed old y_z. For the lower bound
use any new minimizer, which converges to an old y_z by Section 2; its
old objective is nonnegative and its first-order coefficient tends to
the coefficient at that contact. These two bounds prove (16). No
quadratic growth or source-velocity estimate is needed.

For an optional completely linear covariance form define

    J_i^cov=sum_z integral_(boundary K_z)
                [sum_j rho_ij (u_ij.(X-g_z))^2] v_z(X)dS.

Then dot A_i=(D-J_i^cov)/(2M), and (16) becomes

    dot alpha_i=epsilon f_i [min_z C_z(y_z)/(N E_i)
                           +J_i^cov/(2M)-(N+2)D/(2N M)].         (17)

All terms are evaluated on the SAME actual path. The contact minimum
cannot be replaced by a favored source loss.

## 6. Actual covering response and its precise payment obligation

Put

    B_i=sum_j rho_ij/S_ij,
    theta_ij=(rho_ij/S_ij)/B_i.

The regular expansion (11), together with (5) and alpha_i(t)=O(t),
first gives q_i(t)-Q=O(t), then yields

    dot q_i=-sum_j theta_ij L_ij-dot alpha_i/B_i.                 (18)

Consequently the normalized covering derivative is

    d/dt|_0 [q_i(t)/M_t]
       =-[sum_j theta_ij L_ij+dot alpha_i/B_i-beta D]/M.           (19)

If ONE actual compatible path satisfies the strict inequalities

    sum_j theta_ij L_ij+dot alpha_i/B_i > beta D
                                             for every group i, (20)

then (8)--(19) prove an actual decrease of the maximum normalized
buffered depth. All source switches are retained by (3), all old
deepest-base faces are retained by the selected groups, and all other
bases retain their strict gap.

No assertion that (20) always has a solution is made. Under a regular
cap menu the expressions in (20) are finite minima of linear physical
speed functionals, with the same action in every term. Thus this is a
precise additional contact-sensitive response, rather than an
unjustified substitution of an active KKT relation or a single-mark
buffer derivative into the global cover.

For a frozen norm and unnormalized f=E^(1/N), omit dot A_i and the
normalization term D/M in (16). The exact cover construction still
works for signed nonnested paths. For a singleton J_i the minimum
contains one term, but its covariance and mass-normalization terms
remain in the invariant formulation.
